name: Collectivist anarchism
summary: Collectivist anarchism wants the state abolished and land, tools and capital held collectively by workers' associations, federated from the bottom up. Each worker is rewarded according to the labour done rather than according to need, which distinguishes it from anarcho-communism. It looks to trade unions and direct action, and to a popular revolution, as the means, and rejects both parliamentary politics and a Marxist workers' state.
scope: The strand founded by Mikhail Bakunin and developed by the Jura Federation (James Guillaume, Adhemar Schwitzguebel) and Spanish federalist collectivists in the First International era, roughly 1868 to the 1880s. Based on Bakunin's Alliance program and Statism and Anarchy and on the Wikipedia overview. It excludes anarcho-communism after Kropotkin, mutualism, and anarcho-syndicalism, and later issues are answered by inference.

sources.usedFor: State as class rule, Bakunin on God and authority.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Care would come from federated communes and workers' associations rather than a state ministry; inferred from the call to dissolve the state into free associations.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Bakunin treated wage reforms as palliatives that leave capital intact, since only collective ownership of land and capital frees labour; inferred, as the issue is modern.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Capitalist markets are rejected as exploitation, though exchange of products of labour between associations is tolerated; they trust neither officials nor capitalist prices, so a mild disagree, inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Bakunin attacked state ownership (Marx's state bank and state-run industry) as a new form of domination; ownership belongs to workers' associations, not to the state.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Fiscal reform through a state is neither the goal nor opposed; the program goes straight to abolishing inheritance and collectivising capital, so this issue is of little interest.

unions-good.rationale: Trade unions were the main vehicle of social revolution and the nucleus of the post-capitalist society for collectivists.

property-fundamental.rationale: The program makes land and tools collective property used only by workers' associations; private ownership of the means of production is the central target.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Collectivists want capitalist firms abolished and expropriated, not regulated by a state; inferred from their rejection of reformism.

cut-welfare.rationale: No claim that welfare causes dependency; they want to replace charity and state relief with collective ownership and equal conditions, so the cut is not supported; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Land and tools to be collective property of workers' associations is the programmatic core of collectivism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The state is a yoke and an instrument of domination, so extending its powers of control is rejected whatever the justification.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a general hostility to state coercion of adults' private conduct.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: they distrust state censorship and legal repression, while condemning the prejudice itself.

strong-leader.rationale: Bakunin opposed all personal rule and warned that any ruler, even of a People's State, becomes a despot.

state-harmful.rationale: Bakunin held that every state is a yoke and that the state without slavery is unthinkable; it is to be dismantled, not captured.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: a revolutionary tradition that wants the people armed distrusts state disarmament, though no gun policy is stated.

empower-police-military.rationale: Standing armies and police are core instruments of state domination that Bakunin wanted dissolved.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; adherents could see it as free choice or as wage exploitation, so genuinely split.

decide-locally.rationale: Organisation runs from the bottom upward through communes and associations, though economic coordination also needs wider federations.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the program's view that inequalities of upbringing, not nature, produce social ills.

traditional-family.rationale: Bakunin condemned the patriarchal family's despotism of husband and father as an immoral institution.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from equality and opposition to patriarchal control, though they would abolish state marriage itself.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from equality of the sexes and opposition to authority over personal life.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Alliance program declares atheism and seeks abolition of religious cults, replacing divine with human justice.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from its aim of equal conditions for all individuals; no source addresses historical racial redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The program attributes inequality to artificial social conditions and wants equal upbringing for both sexes; inferred for gender specifically.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The program rejects patriotism and Bakunin called nationality a historical local fact rather than a principle, so preserving national tradition is not a goal.

gradual-change.rationale: Bakunin expected a widespread popular revolution involving extensive destruction, not gradual reform of institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The program rests on international working-class solidarity and rejects rivalry between nations.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: bodies of states are hostile, but a federation of free associations on an international scale is wanted.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred: it benefits capital in their view, though they are internationalist.

nation-first.rationale: The program rejects self-styled patriotism and national rivalry in favour of international worker solidarity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Military intervention is by states and armies, which they oppose; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: States are to dissolve into a universal union of free associations, so borders lose their basis.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: nineteenth-century collectivists were committed to science and abundance, and did not raise environmental limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; they would want action by free associations but distrust government action, so unclear.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Bakunin valued science but warned against rule by scientific elites; the statement's optimism is not addressed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; no basis for a position beyond general support for collective control.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bakunin called for an international popular revolution that dismantles the state and would involve a bloody struggle.

experts-over-public.rationale: Bakunin accepted consulting experts but rejected letting them rule or escape criticism.

central-planning.rationale: Bakunin attacked Marx's central state bank and state-directed labour armies, preferring bottom-up federation.

socialized-markets.rationale: Rewards by labour done and exchange between workers' associations leave room for market-like exchange; some disagree, so inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: They would make land collective property rather than leave titles with a tax on them; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The program wants inheritance abolished outright, so heavy taxation points the same direction though falling short.

basic-income.rationale: Collectivists tied reward to labour contributed and wanted no state paymaster; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred: national protection conflicts with international solidarity and state-capitalist interests.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of the economy is the Marxist model Bakunin warned would create a new ruling class.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Collectivists made the collective, not Proudhon's independent small owner, the base unit of property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Collectivists accepted labour-based remuneration; the abolition of wages was the anarcho-communist demand they were contrasted with.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Opposed to state banks, but they do not endorse leaving money to a market; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages and prices embody the statism they reject.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bakunin argued Marxist states would become one-party dictatorships and opposed them.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Alliance program opposes all despotism and accepts only a republican form of government as a transitional stage, so a hereditary monarch has no legitimacy.

democracy-best.rationale: Bakunin called representative government and universal suffrage a lie hiding minority rule, while seeking popular self-organisation instead.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from the stress on power from below, though federal delegation, not referendums, is the stated model.

workers-councils.rationale: Unions and local associations federated from below replace the state as the structure of society, rather than parliaments, though they reject political power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Free federation of associations implies a voluntary union that groups may leave; inferred from the program's federalism.

natural-rulers.rationale: Bakunin rejected any claim that some are fit to rule, including savants and the proletarian elite.

political-violence-never.rationale: He wrote that the problem cannot be solved without a bloody, terrifying struggle.

war-builds-character.rationale: The program rejects national rivalry and patriotism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Atheist and anti-state, they would abolish both cults and the state, so separation is a minimum.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The program replaces divine justice with human justice and seeks abolition of religious cults.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Private courts and defence is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from collectivists' rejection of capitalist and individualist property.

military-superiority.rationale: National military superiority is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's rejection of national rivalry and standing armies (s3).

ethnic-nation.rationale: The program rejects nationalism in favour of universal association.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The working class was seen as the agent of revolutionary change, though Bakunin also stressed state and religion as forces.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The program wants equal starting conditions but enjoyment of goods proportional to production, so adherents hold both equality and unequal reward.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from the idea that land is collective and the peasant ideal that land belongs to the people who work it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialist internationalism; no source addresses reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Bakunin opposed pan-Slavism and pan-Germanism as state-building projects of enslavement.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Freedom is social and mutual for Bakunin; self-interest alone is not the moral basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights and duties are reciprocal for them, but the collective is not placed above the individual; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Nineteenth-century collectivists wrote about society and labour, not environmental ethics, and nothing in their principles settles it either way.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of arguments that blame poverty on numbers rather than property relations.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: they sought to seize industry, not abolish it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; support for science is balanced against distrust of disruptive elites.

human-enhancement.rationale: The question is anachronistic and no principle of collective ownership or anti-statism decides it, so adherents would split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: it concentrates authority in an unaccountable expert apparatus, which Bakunin rejected.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state surveillance and control.

restore-past-order.rationale: They seek a revolutionary new society, not a restored order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred: they hold firm principles about liberty and collective property over pragmatic tests.

direct-action.rationale: Collectivists emphasised direct action and trade-union organising, and rejected reformist parties.

means-match-ends.rationale: Bakunin refused to seize state power because no new power should replace the old, and insisted liberty and socialism go together.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Their programme of collectivising industry and land, and equal education, assumes modern production, and Bakunin championed science.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Bakunin wanted manual labour obligatory for all and wide education, but not an end to specialised roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Bakunin tied reward to labour rather than need, but Guillaume treated collectivism as a transitional stage toward distribution by need, and the statement says 'ultimately', so the answer is contested.

production-for-use.rationale: Collective ownership by workers' associations ends production for capitalist profit; inferred for the use-vs-profit framing.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Bakunin argued that cooperatives cannot free labour while land and capital remain private, implying profit is the exploitation of labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Bakunin argued a people's state under the proletariat would just create a new ruling class.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation of agriculture, about 35-40 percent in Spain in 1936, came from collectivist ideas, though peasants also kept small holdings.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred from their internationalism and view that national rivalry serves ruling classes.

taxation-theft.rationale: They treated the state as exploitative but accepted collective social contributions, unlike individualist anarchists.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from the stress on equal liberty; not stated in sources.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collectivists made the collective, not the individual, the base social unit and property holder.

conscription.rationale: They rejected state armies and would replace them with voluntary arming of the people.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: both exit from a state and its votes leave domination intact; they want abolishing the state.

state-as-business.rationale: Running government as a business is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from collectivists' rejection of both the state and market logic.

positive-liberty.rationale: Liberty needs economic and educational equality; the program binds liberty to collective ownership and equal conditions.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred: Bakunin saw the state and capital as the powers, though he distrusted savants.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The program holds that equal conditions from birth remove artificial inequality and lead to natural equality.

organic-representation.rationale: Federated trade unions and municipalities form the structure, but they reject representation by parties.

total-state.rationale: They oppose the state in every sphere of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Alliance program rejects patriotism and national rivalry, so a campaign for national rebirth is incompatible with working-class internationalism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Expanding one state's reach goes against the program's call for a universal union of free associations and its rejection of national rivalry.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths of loyalty is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's opposition to all despotism and its free federation of associations (s3).

bound-labor.rationale: The program makes the land the property of workers' associations, not lords.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Bakunin accepted science and expert knowledge as legitimate, objecting only to experts ruling.

universal-morality.rationale: The program invokes human justice replacing divine justice; inferred as it is not framed this way.

single-common-good.rationale: Collectivism is a class politics based on the working class against owners, not one reasoned common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of nationalism and the state as such; the question is anachronistic.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from rejecting state-citizenship claims based on nationality.

revive-national-language.rationale: Inferred from rejecting state-led national projects.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' associations running collectively owned enterprises is workplace democracy, though the public as such has no vote.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred: education is to be collective and equal for all children, not market-based.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; state fiscal policy is not their concern.

economic-freedom.rationale: They see liberty needing economic equality, and capitalist economic freedom as subjecting workers; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rejects all rulers, even virtuous ones, because power corrupts.

national-self-determination.rationale: Rejects patriotism and building states, though peoples may organise freely in federation.

force-without-un.rationale: They oppose state military action in general.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The program has science replace faith, though Bakunin also valued revolt and passion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Their solidarity is international, not by citizenship.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Bakunin held labour to be equally obligatory for all, and reward follows one's labour.

class-collaboration.rationale: Collectivism rests on class struggle by workers against capital.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Bakunin said destruction is creative but wanted universal education; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred: they favour a workers' international over fronts of states.

workers-nation.rationale: The program insists on international working-class solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The program demands political, economic and social equality of both sexes and equal upbringing for boys and girls, which leaves no room for legally distinct roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Opposed to income from capital but not for legal prohibition by a state; adherents unclear.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: They oppose all legal hierarchies and aim at equality.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state implies one class dominating another, a view Bakunin held directly.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy was not a concern; collective ownership of industry could back either choice, so this is inferred as neutral.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from international solidarity and rejection of nationalism.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiratorial nationalist claim at odds with their internationalism; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: They rejected parliamentary politics in favour of direct action and unions.

national-mission.rationale: A mission to spread one nation's government abroad conflicts with the program's rejection of patriotism and its aim of dissolving states.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Bakunin condemned the despotism of husband and father as built into the family institution.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Bakunin held that those who rule, including workers who become rulers, come to look down on the masses.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic limits on reproduction is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's opposition to coercion and its view that inequality is artificial (s3).

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from hostility to armies and police.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They oppose the state entirely, including defending property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Marriage across racial lines is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's rejection of nationalism and inequality (s3).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The program seeks equality of individuals and classes, though they reject law as such.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred: Bakunin sought an international uprising.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from equality and secularism; they would not endorse a state code.

restrict-conversion.rationale: They oppose religion but also state coercion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religiously motivated state ban conflicts with atheism and anti-statism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The program seeks atheism, science replacing faith, and equal education.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Bakunin said a workers' state would not wither and denounced strengthening states.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The program favours free association; consent in principle, but they reject the state altogether.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred: a mercantilist aim contrary to internationalism.

population-transfer.rationale: Expelling minorities is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's rejection of nationalism and coercion (s3).

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Bakunin accepted violence and mass destruction of property in revolution.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Their economics rests on solidarity and collective property rather than competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: State suppression of parties is a state power they reject.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Bakunin saw the state and slavery as inseparable, and domination as unfreedom even without abuse.

separated-powers.rationale: Divided state powers still leave a state; they favour dissolving it.

vanguard-party.rationale: Bakunin favoured spontaneous worker action over a working-class party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Bakunin looked to the poorest workers and peasants as the base of the revolution.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Extends private property in the means of life, instead of collective ownership.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes and union direct action are their core method.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: They attribute poverty to property and inheritance, not numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Their internationalism treats such claims as nationalist.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; they reject offices, so unclear.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Bakunin saw the state as an instrument of domination, and emergency powers would extend that domination over its internal opponents.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A state measure that leaves capitalism intact; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Bakunin warned that Marxist rule would become a one-party dictatorship, and control of information by such a party is part of what he feared.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the army is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the movement's opposition to standing armies and party dictatorship (s2).

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The program's international working-class solidarity treats citizenship barriers between workers as artificial divisions.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from their view that rulers become privileged.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: They rejected parties for federated autonomy.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: A union of states is not their model, though anti-nationalist.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Bakunin opposed concentrating command of armies and ministers in one person, since standing armies and rulers are what the revolution is meant to abolish.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church government is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the Alliance's call to abolish religious cults (s3); church polity is moot for it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's atheism and replacement of divine by human justice (s3).

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The program rejects patriotism and rivalry between nations in favour of international worker solidarity, so workers should not back their own state in a great-power war, though a defeatist policy is not stated.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral censorship of art is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bakunin's view that state coercion always serves domination (s2).

unlimited-reelection.rationale: They reject presidencies and permanent rulers altogether, so this is an inferred mild disagreement rather than a stated position.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from federalism from below and distrust of rulers.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred from rejecting militarism and national rivalry.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred: they favour collective not household ownership of the means of production.

people-in-arms.rationale: Bakunin attacked state-controlled armies and wanted the people to defend the revolution.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: He criticised the village commune's patriarchal domination; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunifying a nation as a state is a statist, nationalist project; the program prefers a universal federation, though nothing addresses divided nations specifically.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Distrust of savants is balanced by their commitment to universal education.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from the program's rejection of national rivalry and its equal footing for all individuals and peoples.

death-penalty.rationale: Bakunin held that the state rests on violence over the governed, and execution is its ultimate form, though he accepted revolutionary violence against rulers.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the program's equal education for children of both sexes from birth; sex education itself is not mentioned.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Creationism in public schools is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the Alliance programme's atheism and its replacement of faith by science (s3).

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred: legal restriction of private conduct hands moral power to the state, which they distrust, though the subject is not addressed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Tying political membership to ancestry runs against the rejection of patriotism and the universal union of free associations.

minority-language-support.rationale: Federal autonomy for communes and peoples would let them use their own languages; support is inferred, not stated.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; hostile to religion, but also to laws.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from Bakunin's insistence on liberty.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The program accepts only political action aimed at workers' victory over capital.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Collectivists rejected reformist parliamentary politics in favour of union action, so an elected assembly is not their route; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Trading freedoms for growth is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bakunin's claim that socialism without liberty becomes domination (s2).

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Solidarity is internationalist but they would not rely on state aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement and is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bakunin's opposition to standing armies and state military power.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: They reject having a head of state at all, so an elected one is at best the lesser evil; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A state-linked central bank is part of the machinery of domination he criticised in Marx's plan for a state bank; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Insisting on historic homeland territory is the nationalism the program rejects.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: They reject private ownership of land and capital rather than accept it with limits.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Bakunin predicted a red bureaucracy as a new ruling class; the Soviet case is anachronistic.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; collective ownership alone does not settle how to treat uncertain environmental risk.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliances bind states into armed blocs, against the program's rejection of national rivalry and standing armies.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from rejection of conquest and national domination; annexation specifically is not discussed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Hostile to the church, but also to state authority over clergy.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A symbolic head of state is still a state institution, and the state is to be dissolved.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The program calls for free federation of associations, which depends on voluntary union rather than armed retention.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Federal autonomy for associations and regions is the model, so this is inferred as agreeable although the case is a modern one.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred head of state is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's atheism and opposition to despotism (s3).

flat-income-tax.rationale: A flat tax favours the wealthy relative to progressive rates and leaves capital untouched; inferred, since taxation is not discussed.

character-from-environment.rationale: The program expects equal conditions from birth to remove artificial inequalities.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The program opposes all despotism, which is rule not bound by law or the governed.

space-expansion.rationale: The issue is anachronistic and collectivist principles do not settle it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mixed constitutions is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bakunin's rejection of every form of state rule (s2).

leader-cult.rationale: Bakunin opposed personal rule and warned that those who rule come to look down on the masses.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law presumptions are not discussed; equality of sexes is stated but the court presumption is a separate matter.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Bakunin held that rulers form a new class; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land is to become collective property for those who work it, rather than distributed to individuals.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of nationalism and of the state boundaries that block movement.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims for co-nationals is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's rejection of national rivalry (s3).

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Atheist and opposed to coercion, they would never punish leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress laws is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's demand for equality of the sexes (s3).

common-currency.rationale: A shared currency among states preserves state monetary authority; inferred mild disagreement.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Bakunin rejected pan-Slavism, arguing a Slavic empire would only enslave Slavic peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Federal autonomy for peoples and associations fits this, but the specific question of national minorities is inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from internationalism; minorities should struggle with the workers around them rather than found a nation-state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Bakunin stressed economic conditions but disputed Marx's primacy.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred: state competition policy leaves capital intact.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from hostility to state aid to capital.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They reject both courts and majority state rule.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: They reject state bodies; equality is wanted.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: A closed imperial bloc contradicts the call for international workers' solidarity and a universal union of associations.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; standards set by state agreements are not their method, but they would favour workers' protection.

moral-incentives.rationale: The program ties enjoyment of goods to each person's production.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Collectivists preferred trade union organising to small violent groups.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The program begins with the abolition of inheritance.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nation-centred history teaching serves the patriotism the program rejects; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: They oppose domination of one group by another.

patriotic-education.rationale: The program rejects self-styled patriotism, and Bakunin wanted education to be integral and universal rather than nationalist.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from the stress on equal conditions for all; the issue is a modern one.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation by a public body is a state function, but collectivists did not address monetary mechanisms beyond collectivisation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: They expected revolution from capitalism's contradictions.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Influence in former imperial regions is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the movement's rejection of national rivalry.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; international solidarity favours worker exchange, but delinking is a modern debate.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred from their view that all workers are exploited.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The program seeks equality of individuals and classes, which excludes a right of owners to exclude people at will.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: A constitutional order of state courts and law is still a state; inferred mild disagreement.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state boundaries and imperial domination; treaties themselves are not discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Alliance accepts only a republican form where states persist.

minority-veto.rationale: Federated groups may decide by majority within autonomy.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Bakunin saw all rulers as legitimate targets of revolt, so resisting a ruler who breaks the rules is a weaker form of his stance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Bakunin called representative government a fiction that hides minority rule; though better than monarchy, it is not their model.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from the humanitarian emphasis on ending suffering and domination.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed, and adherents could go either way, so neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duty of privilege is replaced by abolishing privilege.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The program requires active political and revolutionary commitment aimed at workers' victory over capital.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Bakunin saw religion and institutions pacifying; modern media inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Bakunin linked state rule to religion and ideology as well as force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the view that capital exploits labour; international transfers between countries are not discussed.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving public office for the native-born is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's internationalism and rejection of patriotism (s3).

party-own-road.rationale: Federal autonomy and mistrust of centralised parties suggest each movement chooses its own road; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; adherents might favour mutual aid between peoples or local self-reliance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Reclaiming lost territory is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's rejection of national rivalry (s3).

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: they oppose any group ruling another, and a group of descendants holding leadership over another group would be one.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from opposition to despotism and nationalism; fascism was later than collectivism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anti-authoritarian but would reject equivalence in class terms.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from Bakunin's view that the state and slavery are tied together; the Civil War is not discussed.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the revolutionary rejection of inherited authority and rulers' honours.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources say nothing about this; equality of the sexes is stated, but not how to weigh specific disadvantages.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the program's equality of the sexes and condemnation of domination in the family.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Bakunin rejected states of all kinds and was universalist about liberty, so cultural relativism about government is not his stance.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A guardian role for the army is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bakunin's attack on standing armies as tools of state domination (s2).

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the principle that goods are enjoyed in proportion to labour contributed, which would cover domestic labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Bakunin condemned the despotism of the father as immoral, so lifelong duty to parents is not their ideal.

office-by-exam.rationale: Bakunin rejected rule by those with learning.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: A state blocking firm purchases protects owners rather than workers; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from Bakunin's condemnation of the husband's despotism and the program's equality of the sexes.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Power from below needs delegates answerable to those who chose them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Individual capitalism instead of collective provision.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land becomes collective property used by workers' associations.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Bakunin rejected parliamentary representation as a fiction hiding minority rule.

single-official-language.rationale: Federation of free associations means autonomy of peoples, not one language imposed from above.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign land ownership is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from the programme's plan for land held by workers' associations regardless of nationality (s3).

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A legal doctrine not addressed by collectivists, and they would doubt state adjudication.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from a critique of capitalism and production for profit, though not stated.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: State proxy wars are national rivalry carried out by armed state means.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc intervention is not discussed in the sources; the answer is inferred from Bakunin's opposition to states ruling other peoples.

corporate-influence.rationale: Bakunin held that the state serves privileged classes, and capital's influence over government follows from this.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: A state pretext of sovereignty for controlling civil society contradicts international solidarity and anti-statism.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: State population policy is statist and tied to nationalism, which they reject; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Restricting purchases by residence status is nationalist and exclusionary; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state employer of last resort keeps wage labour under state control, unlike collective ownership by workers.

democratic-peace.rationale: Bakunin doubted that representative democracies are really popular rule, so spreading them is not the route to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Bakunin said if God existed it would be necessary to abolish him; authority has no inherent claim.

industrial-unions.rationale: Trade-union federations were the nucleus of the new society, and industry-wide organisation fits their federal model; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Collectivist internationalism and equality reject claims that a minority conspires against the nation, though Bakunin's own writings include prejudiced remarks.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Bakunin's attack on the patriarchal family; the program itself does not address marriage law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state secrecy and rule by a privileged minority.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; federation of local associations suggests it, but exchange across federations also fits.

informal-organisation.rationale: Collectivists organised via unions and federations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: They reject the supremacy of any state's law, and international solidarity favours worker federation over national law; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The program declares atheism and rejects patriotism, so defining the nation by a religion is rejected.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Alliance program rejects patriotism and every state, so no state has a claim to deference.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from federation of free associations that pool resources through solidarity, not regional self-interest.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Collectivism holds land, tools and capital in common while workers are paid for their labour, so personal goods are not collective.

defeat-communism.rationale: Bakunin attacked authoritarian communism but was a socialist revolutionary; he was not interested in defeating communism, so this is inferred as strong disagreement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Collectivists wanted services run by workers associations, not by the state or private owners; inferred from federated ownership.

religion-illusion.rationale: Bakunin was an atheist who held that religion consoled the poor and would pass with social equality and education.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Bakunin did not accept Marx stage theory; inferred that he judged capitalism an exploitative system to be overthrown.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Alliance program demanded equality of the sexes together with abolition of inheritance and collective property.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the program making children education and maintenance a collective duty; domestic services are not mentioned.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Bakunin rejection of patriotism and nationalist purity.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; collectivists reject the state, so treaties between a state and a nation are not their concern.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Collectivist anarchism wants federations of self-governing workers associations holding property collectively.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Bakunin rejection of nationalism and patriotism and opposition to state steering of populations.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Collectivists reject capitalism and the Marxist workers state; whether that is a third way is inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Bakunin rejected nationalist state claims in favour of free federations of peoples; inferred that historic title would not outweigh present inhabitants.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; an egalitarian internationalist movement is inferred to reject it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement opposed state coercion of individuals, inferred to extend to private sexual conduct.

suppress-opposition.rationale: It wants the state abolished as an instrument of class rule, so using it to suppress opposition is the reverse of its aim.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Alliance program was militantly atheist, abolishing state-backed cults, and rejected any coercive state; punishing blasphemy is opposed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Opposed domination by states over peoples and the exploitation of labour; inferred rejection of colonial rule.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not a doctrine of the movement, which is atheist; inferred rejection of a religious-duty framing, though resistance to invasion would be supported.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: It supports revolution against rulers but on social, not religious-law grounds; inferred rejection of the statement as worded.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Bottom-up federation of workers' associations and direct action through unions mean decisions are made by people directly in workplaces and communities.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Class oppression is central and the Alliance program demanded equality of the sexes; inferred sympathy with joint struggle, though race was not addressed.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the principle of individual freedom against state coercion.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its emphasis on individual freedom and rejection of religious authority.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: It is a socialist current that rejected both state socialism and liberalism rather than blending left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Workers are held to be exploited by capital and separated from the product and control of their labour, which collective ownership is meant to end; the term itself is Marxian.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Anachronistic; an internationalist, anti-nationalist and atheist movement would reject civilizational incompatibility claims.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Bakunin's program states atheism and rejects all authority from God or the state.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from its anti-clerical atheism; it wants no state at all, but where one exists it should be free of religious cult.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from hostility to employer power over workers.

social-market-economy.rationale: It rejects both laissez-faire and any state-run economy, seeking collective ownership by federated workers' associations.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: It abolishes the state and standing armies, favouring popular armed militias, so adherents lean toward abolition but not pacifism.

rich-first.rationale: Collective property and equality of classes and individuals leave no room for letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and rejection of states' power politics; the movement had no policy on blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Bakunin demanded abolition of the state and of all hereditary rights, including inheritance of position, in the Alliance program.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Collectivists wanted capital held collectively and credit run by federated workers' associations, which approximates user-owned credit; the explicit at-cost form is closer to mutualism, so inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Opposed to states and bourgeois finance alike, so conditions imposed by international lenders would be resisted, though it rejects governments as the actors; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement rejected parliamentary politics and the bourgeois state, and above all class privilege in political rights, as stated in Statism and Anarchy.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The Alliance program demanded the equality of the sexes, but the nature-domination link is a later ecofeminist idea; inferred and split.

reification.rationale: Bakunin held that capital and the market rule over workers, a close cousin of commodity fetishism, though the term is Marxist and Bakunin opposed Marx; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Bakunin argued that political liberties are fictions for workers while the bourgeoisie holds economic power, which the statement restates.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Bakunin rejected state law and rulers entirely, though he accepted free federal agreements; the statement presumes rulers, so adherents are split.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Alliance program called for equality of all and Bakunin denounced nationalism and exclusive privileges; a racial franchise contradicts it.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; collectivists favoured direct, federated participation but rejected deciding within state structures; inferred and split.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; collectivists abolish the state, so government records are not their concern, though they favour openness in federated bodies.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Bakunin demanded abolition of religious marriage and free unions, and was militantly anti-religious.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Bakunin opposed religious and national prejudice and called for international solidarity of workers.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Anachronistic; it rejected state decision-making, so a state-convened assembly is out, though federated direct decision-making would be familiar; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Bakunin sought the abolition of religion as authority rather than its reform, so reinterpreting doctrine misses the point.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Alliance program calls for abolishing inheritance and making property collective because economic inequality destroys liberty for the majority.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from opposition to authority and moral coercion, though the movement did not address it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Alliance program wants atheism and science in place of faith, but a collectivist anarchist rejects any state running education, so the statement's mechanism is opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Collectivists abolish the state and its coercive machinery, replacing it with federated workers' associations and communes that handle social order.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of state structures; communities would federate freely rather than share state executive power.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Care is meant to flow from workers' associations and federated communes as of right, not from charity, which Bakunin disliked; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; collectivists reject parliamentary politics altogether, so limiting terms in office is largely beside the point.

vote-delegation.rationale: Bakunin's federation from below with recallable delegates is inferred to favour revocable mandates over fixed representation.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources do not discuss it, so adherents' view is inferred as indifferent.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Alliance program demands equality of the sexes, so equal eligibility for religious office follows, though collectivists want religion abolished.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Alliance program demands equality of the sexes and rejects the husband's legal authority over the wife.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the First International's internationalism and rejection of nation-state membership; collectivists would not tie participation to citizenship.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: collectivists want housing held collectively and the state abolished, so a state-enforced cap is not their remedy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from collective ownership of the means of production and rewards for labour rather than ownership; exclusive private rights over ideas fit poorly with that.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Bakunin opposed the state, militarism and national service, so state-drilled uniformed youth movements are the opposite of free federated association.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from hostility to the state and its armies; the issue postdates the strand.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from opposition to states, standing armies and foreign domination; the issue postdates the strand.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Adherents would condemn mass killings but not look to governments for formal recognition; inferred and split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Collectivism's defining rule is that each is rewarded for the labour done, with capital held collectively so ownership yields no income.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Bakunin championed popular revolution and revolutionary violence, so a rule against all killing is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Bakunin rejected nationalism and the state in favour of international federation of free associations.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The strand predates this debate; it asserted sexual equality but took no known view on whether sex is constructed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic to the strand; its program demands equal conditions for both sexes without addressing the category of women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Bakunin was an atheist hostile to nationalism, so honouring national martyrs as saints runs against both.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Bakunin's materialist atheism treated politics as a struggle over class and authority, not a spiritual contest of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Nation and homeland are not categories the strand uses; inferred indifference.

culture-before-state.rationale: The strand seeks to abolish the state rather than build one, but gives no view on cultural renewal; inferred and split.

god-not-male.rationale: Bakunin rejected God altogether, so the description of God is not an issue for the strand; inferred indifference.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: Bakunin attacked religious authority and demanded equal conditions for both sexes, so he would favour judging religion by human emancipation.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Alliance program demands equality of classes and individuals and the end of national privilege, which excludes ethnic ownership.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: it favours bottom-up federation by free association rather than merging regions into national units.

independent-unions.rationale: Collectivists looked to trade unions as the organs of the revolution and of future production, independent of any state or party.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Bakunin rejected the Marxist workers' state but held that the workers must themselves control production and society.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from collective ownership of land and capital by federated associations; local services would be collectively run.

second-chamber.rationale: Collectivists reject parliamentary politics and the state, and a bottom-up federation has no upper chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Property is held by workers' associations, not strictly by the local community; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Collectivists federate from the bottom up, with delegates bound by the associations that send them.

family-wage.rationale: Rewards follow labour done rather than need, which distinguishes collectivism from anarcho-communism.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the aim of abolishing the state's power over individuals and associations.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from Bakunin's stress on individual freedom, which he said is realised through others' freedom.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Alliance program declared for atheism and materialism, so spiritual needs are not a political task.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Power flows upward from free communes in a federation, so a central legislature cannot withdraw it.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement was internationalist and organised by class, not race.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of nationalism and national states.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to state wars and standing armies in favour of popular militias.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from Bakunin's federalism of free communes, which opposed state nationalism, though he backed the self-determination of peoples.

communal-electorates.rationale: The strand rejects parliamentary and electoral politics altogether, so separate religious electorates have no place.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from the stress on class over nation; plots between states are seen as ruling-class rivalry, not a threat to a people.

free-public-college.rationale: The Alliance program demands equal education and training for all children, which implies tuition-free provision through associations.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from rejection of the state as a taxing authority; the strand expects collective ownership, not taxes, to curb abuse.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from collective stewardship of land and tools; the strand did not discuss ecology.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The strand argued for equality of the sexes, not distinct values, so extra weight for one is inferred to be rejected.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the strand's opposition to standing armies and militarism; reduction is a step toward abolition.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from hostility to state secrecy and ruling-class diplomacy; the strand wanted no state deals at all.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the aim to abolish the state and collectivize capital, which leaves no state to control its flow.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Bakunin sought abolition of the state and its army and police, to be replaced by federated associations and the armed people.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Bakunin rejected patriotism and state wars as serving rulers, though he accepted revolutionary war, so refusal is agreed with.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Collectivists looked to unions and group action by workers, but sought abolition of the wage system; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: State top-ups are palliatives that leave capital intact and rely on the state; inferred from Bakunin's view of reforms.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Anarchists reject legal state rules over a state they want abolished; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The programme is the abolition of capitalism and the state, not reform of world economic rules; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Bakunin states that the state must be destroyed and not seized, against Marx's workers' state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Collectivists specified collective property and reward by labour, but federated units were left free to organise; adherents are split, inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; collective ownership implies no pricing of nature as capital, inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Alliance program rejects patriotism and the nation as a state-made abstraction.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents opposed privilege and exploitation, so cancelling a burden is inferred to be welcome.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Bakunin opposed centralized states exploiting provinces and favoured federation; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Bakunin was a materialist who saw humans as socially made, yet affirmed equality; adherents have no stated view.

public-service-media.rationale: Anarchists reject state-run institutions, but media is not discussed; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Bakunin's Alliance program is militantly atheist and treats all religion as the enslavement of humanity, so no religion expresses a truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Collectivists reject a state buying or guaranteeing crop prices; land belongs to the agricultural workers' federated associations instead.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear weapons did not exist, but the movement wanted the state and its armies abolished; inferred from anti-statism and anti-militarism.

workers-own-party.rationale: Collectivists rejected parliamentary politics and any workers' party, as Bakunin attacked Marx's electoral approach, and relied on unions and direct action.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed and anarchists reject state prohibition, but they opposed harm to women; inferred from the program's equality of the sexes, so a mild agree.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Alliance program demands equality of the sexes, but also abolishes inheritance, so women's equal right to inherit land does not arise as such; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not a collectivist concern; the movement was internationalist and rejected nationality as a basis, so no position is inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Collective ownership by federated associations would settle harms through collective rules, not individual lawsuits or agencies; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Bakunin rejected all authority and hereditary rule, so an official role for chiefs in national law is opposed.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement valued freedom as central and would not subordinate it to a state-enforced priority; inferred from Bakunin's view of freedom.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Collectivists wanted courts and the state's penal system abolished, so fixed legal sentences are rejected.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The program rejects patriotism and nation-states and favours free federation, so state-imposed national language requirements are opposed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Collectivists build on voluntary workers' associations and reject compulsion; inferred, though they also expect all workers to join federated associations.

voter-id.rationale: Bakunin rejects bourgeois elections and the state altogether, so state rules policing the ballot would be opposed as more state machinery; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Alliance program demands abolition of all state-backed cults, so no interpretation can have legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Statism and Anarchy attacks universal suffrage and representative government as rule by a privileged class; democracy requires real popular self-rule and equality.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Alliance program calls for equality of the sexes and free choice in union, and rejects church marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state control and the call to abolish the state; no stated position on communications.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anarchists would abolish wages and the state's taxation and welfare for collective property; inferred from that.

women-suffrage.rationale: Bakunin demands equal rights for women but rejects voting and office-holding itself, so the statement fits poorly; adherents reject both.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Bakunin saw religion as a main support of authority including the patriarchal family, and the Alliance program demanded equality of the sexes with abolition of religious marriage.

race-social-construct.rationale: Bakunin rejected racial hierarchy but also used national-character claims, so inferred from his universalism.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Collectivists would oppose state ministries on principle and seek equality through society's own federations; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The Alliance program demands collective ownership of land and capital by workers' associations, which rules out private appropriation by first claim.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: Bakunin rejected state authority and its legal apparatus, so a state-created court system sits badly with the doctrine, though accountability for atrocity would be welcomed.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Bakunin's anarchism was explicitly atheist and opposed to divine authority, so scriptural inerrancy is rejected.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine demands equality of the sexes and abolition of the patriarchal family, which supports guaranteeing gender equality in any self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Bakunin rejected the Marxist workers' state and warned that a ruling bureaucracy would form a new exploiting class, so defending such a state is rejected.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: collectivists favored federation from below with mandated and recallable delegates, but also rejected hierarchical office, so delegated election of higher offices is only partly fitting.

national-church-status.rationale: Bakunin's program opposes all state churches and religious authority and demands the abolition of the state and of official cults.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Bakunin's federalism recognised the right of each people and region to self-determination and autonomy within a free federation.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: free self-determination of communities by their own inhabitants fits federalist principles, though the doctrine rejects states and nations as units.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine denies the legitimacy of states and borders, so it neither endorses colonial borders nor a nationalist redrawing.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: collectivism aimed at abundant collective production and rewarded labour, rather than asceticism or limited needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the First International-era doctrine did not address indigenous peoples; it opposed state restriction in general but supported local self-rule.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from its demand for full equality of the sexes; the doctrine rejects the standing army and conscription, so applying it to neither also fits.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Bakunin rejected the patriotism of the state and nation, and the movement was internationalist, so no sacred duty to a national homeland.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The movement opposed state violence and police powers; inferred, as drug policing was not an issue of its era.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anarchists oppose state diplomacy and economic alliances between states altogether; inferred from the call to abolish the state.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Bakunin opposed state action on behalf of nationals abroad as statism and held that peoples should federate freely.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Alliance program says land and capital must be collective property of workers' associations, so those holding them owe the whole society.

self-ownership.rationale: Collectivists prized individual liberty yet held that the products of labour belong to associations and that no one is free alone; split.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Any state taxation is opposed and consumption taxes fall hardest on workers; inferred from the call to abolish the state.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Collectivists reject state-run welfare, targeted or not, in favour of associations; leaning against targeting inferred from equality principle.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Collectivists relied on trade unions, federations and associations as the base of society and rejected top leaders.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The program abolishes the state and class privilege, so state favours to firms would be refused outright.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Bakunin was an avowed atheist who called for the abolition of churches and religious influence on public life.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The movement looked forward to revolution and science, and rejected tradition and authority; inferred and anachronistic.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Alliance program called for the abolition of religious marriage and for women's equality, so a wife could end the marriage freely.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resources should be held by workers' associations, not by any national state, though the target is also foreign capital; inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Collectivists reward only labour done and abolish inheritance and private capital, judging distribution by a pattern rather than by who acquired it.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; collectivists sought to abolish capitalism, not to tax it, so no stance can be inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from Bakunin's view that all systems of inequality and domination persist and must be overthrown.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from Bakunin's view that the state and its laws are illegitimate instruments of domination and justice comes from society.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic; collectivists wanted workers to own tools and be rewarded by labour, with no stated view on automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Collectivists were internationalist and sought abolition of states, not a balance among powers, so the question does not fit.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Collectivists reward each worker by the labour done and hold that capital is created by labour, in the line of the First International's labour economics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Bakunin rejected patriotism and the nation state as tools of rulers and favoured the federation of free workers across borders.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: collectivists centred on the workers' economic struggle but also opposed all authority, including on identity grounds, and no stance is stated.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Bakunin rejected both the state and a party-led workers' state, calling the Marxist state a new tyranny.

missingStatements.text: The right to inherit property should be abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: The Alliance program says equality begins with the abolition of inheritance; existing statements cover only hereditary titles and taxation.

missingStatements.text: Each person's share of goods should be proportional to the labour they contribute.
missingStatements.rationale: Collectivism's defining distribution rule is enjoyment of goods according to each person's own production, set against distribution by need.

missingStatements.text: All children should receive the same maintenance, education and training from birth, whatever their parents' means.
missingStatements.rationale: Point three of the Alliance program makes equal conditions for children of both sexes the basis for removing artificial inequality.

notes: Anarcho-communists criticised collectivist wage-based remuneration, and Guillaume treated collectivism as transitional toward distribution by need. Bakunin's writings contain prejudiced remarks and conspiratorial elements. Many answers on modern issues are inferred (low confidence). Wikipedia pages were read only for their first 100,000 characters.
